general.reason: Sec. 2.1 and Appendix A prove that the ExTernD residual decreases monotonically and can be driven below any ε > 0, which is a claim about post-training factorization capacity. Sec. 5 then says "our structural and representational claims against them [refs 5, 2] are proven (Sec. 2.1)", but ref [2] (BitNet 1.58) is a training-from-scratch method, and the convergence proof for post-training fixed-weight factorization does not constrain what a jointly trained ternary model can represent — the paper provides no theorem or argument that applies to trained models.

evidence.claim: The Limitations claim that structural/representational claims against BitNet 1.58 are proven overstates Sec. 2.1; the stated proof only applies to fixed-plane PTQ, not to BitNet-style end-to-end trained models.
evidence.excerpt: Sec. 5 asserts: "our structural and representational claims against them [refs 5, 2] are proven (Sec. 2.1)". Sec. 2.1 (and Appendix A) prove convergence ... a valid capacity argument against fixed-plane PTQ (i.e. PTQTP, ref [5]), but ref [2] is The Era of 1-bit LLMs, a training-from-scratch method: ... no post-training factorization theorem constrains it.

judge_panel.reason: Sec. 2.1 and Appendix A prove that the ExTernD residual decreases monotonically and can be driven below any ε > 0, which is a claim about post-training factorization capacity. Sec. 5 then says "our structural and representational claims against them [refs 5, 2] are proven (Sec. 2.1)", but ref [2] (BitNet 1.58) is a training-from-scratch method, and the convergence proof for post-training fixed-weight factorization does not constrain what a jointly trained ternary model can represent — the paper provides no theorem or argument that applies to trained models.

The paper says in Limitations that “our structural and representational claims against them [5, 2] are proven (Sec. 2.1),” but the actual result in Appendix A is only the representational statement that “No fixed number of ternary planes has this property; the expansion is what removes the information bottleneck.” That proves a capacity claim about fixed-plane representations, not BitNet-style end-to-end trained models in ref. [2].

The paper claims in Section 5 that "our structural and representational claims against them [5, 2] are proven (Sec. 2.1)". However, as the reviewer correctly notes, Section 2.1 and Appendix A only prove the convergence of the residual for the post-training factorization algorithm, which mathematically applies to PTQ but does not constrain the representational capacity of a model trained from scratch like BitNet (Ref [2]).

general.reason: Sec. 3.6 states "utilizing Shannon entropy to account for zero-density" but then arrives at 6.68 bpw for PTQTP K=4 at ~33% sparsity, which is exactly 4×(2−0.33)=6.68 from the mask+sign packing formula in Eq. (5). Shannon entropy of a 33% sparse Bernoulli mask would give H(0.33)≈0.917 bits per mask bit, yielding a different (lower) number, so the terminology "Shannon entropy" is incorrect for the calculation actually performed.

evidence.claim: The Iso-BPW parity paragraph in Sec. 3.6 invokes 'Shannon entropy' but the 6.68 bpw figure is the mask+sign packing formula from Eq. (5), not an entropy calculation.
evidence.excerpt: Sec. 3.6 says "A fairer comparison matches the effective bits-per-weight (BPW), utilizing Shannon entropy to account for zero-density. PTQTP at K = 4 (∼33% sparsity) requires 6.68 effective BPW." But 6.68 = 4·(2 − 0.33) is exactly the mask+sign packing bound in Eq. (5)... Either the terminology should be corrected to "mask+sign packing (Eq. 5)", or the 6.68 number should be recomputed under an entropy-coded model — the two are not the same...

judge_panel.reason: Sec. 3.6 states "utilizing Shannon entropy to account for zero-density" but then arrives at 6.68 bpw for PTQTP K=4 at ~33% sparsity, which is exactly 4×(2−0.33)=6.68 from the mask+sign packing formula in Eq. (5). Shannon entropy of a 33% sparse Bernoulli mask would give H(0.33)≈0.917 bits per mask bit, yielding a different (lower) number, so the terminology "Shannon entropy" is incorrect for the calculation actually performed.

Sec. 3.6 says the comparison matches BPW by “utilizing Shannon entropy to account for zero-density,” yet the paper’s explicit BPW formula is the mask+sign packing rule “bpweff = … · (2 − sparsity)” (Eq. 5), and it separately notes this packing is only “near the entropy floor.” Thus the cited “6.68 effective BPW” is presented as entropy-based even though the paper defines BPW via Eq. (5), not Shannon entropy.

Section 3.6 explicitly claims to be "utilizing Shannon entropy to account for zero-density" when calculating that PTQTP at K = 4 (33% sparsity) "requires 6.68 effective BPW." The reviewer correctly identifies that 6.68 is exactly the result of the mask+sign packing formula (4 * (2 - 0.33) = 6.68) introduced in Eq. 5, not a Shannon entropy calculation, making the text factually inaccurate.
